record.field: Run Payroll — your first pay run
Create one month of draft payslips for one division, and know what you have and have not just done.

Picking a division here does more than filter a list of people: it selects the formula configuration every payslip in this run will be computed by. Choose the wrong one and every number downstream is wrong in the same direction, which is the hardest kind of error to spot.
The configuration and its version are printed in the scope panel on the right. Read them before you compute, not after.
You have computed July and one payslip has an overtime figure that looks far too high. What do you do?
Fix the overtime in the source data, then recompute the run.
Exactly. Payslips are an output. Correct the input that produced them and recompute, and the whole run stays consistent with the data behind it.
Edit the net amount on that payslip so it looks right.
Let's rethink that. Editing the output leaves the input still wrong, so the next recompute silently undoes your fix — and the payslip no longer agrees with the attendance record behind it.
